segments.narration: A masked man hijacked Chicago television for ninety seconds. November 1987, mid-episode, a Doctor Who rerun dissolved into static and a grinning plastic face.
He rocked before a sheet of corrugated metal, buzzing distorted nonsense. Two hours earlier the same face had seized WGN for seventeen seconds.
How do you hijack a television station from outside the building? Engineers at WGN killed it in seconds. WTTW's tower sat unmanned.
The method was brute force: a microwave signal aimed at the broadcast tower, stronger than the station's own, overpowering it.
That needed real broadcast gear and real expertise. The FCC investigated anyway and found nobody. The statute of limitations expired in 1992.

verdicts.claim: On 22 November 1987 an unknown person in a Max Headroom mask interrupted Chicago TV broadcasts, including roughly 90 seconds over WTTW during a Doctor Who serial.
verdicts.note: 89% of the claim's wording appears in the reference article, including 3 number(s)

verdicts.claim: The earlier intrusion that night hit WGN-TV at about 9:14 p.m. and showed the masked figure for nearly 17 seconds.
verdicts.note: Both sources give the 9:14 p.m. WGN time and the 'nearly 17 seconds' figure. Narration rounds to 'seventeen seconds'.

verdicts.claim: WGN engineers regained control of their signal within seconds, while WTTW's transmitter site had nobody on duty, so the second intrusion ran much longer.
verdicts.note: 80% of the claim's wording appears in the reference article

verdicts.claim: The hijack worked by sending a more powerful microwave transmission to the stations' broadcast towers than the stations themselves were sending, triggering a capture effect.
verdicts.note: Wikipedia describes exactly this mechanism. Narration simplifies 'capture effect' to 'overpowering it'.

verdicts.claim: The FCC's criminal investigation never identified the perpetrators and the statute of limitations expired in 1992.
verdicts.note: Both sources confirm the FCC investigation failed and the perpetrators have never been positively identified; Wikipedia gives the 1992 expiry.
